messages:
samir: FYI — after rolling runtime v2.13.0 to shard eu-west-1-a at ~10:12 UTC we're seeing p95 up ~2.4x and p99 ~3.8x on text-generation (sync/generate). Customers reported timeouts and very long tails. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/inference/d/abcd/perf-overview :eyes:

olivia: saw the alert. error rates OK, no obvious 5xx spike, mostly latency. Any deploy tags or config diffs besides the runtime binary?

samir: only things in the rollout: kernel-selector tweak + default batching window reduced from 12ms->6ms. Release note: "aggressive latebinding + kernel selector improvements". No config flips besides that.

ops-bot: ALERT: p99 latency increased from 220ms -> 840ms across shard eu-west-1-a in the last 3m. Route health still green.

kerry: can someone run quick bisect on the rollout cohort? If kernel selector is suspect, try routing a small cohort to previous kernel path.

ravi: starting cohort split now — directing 10% traffic back to runtime v2.12.8 on eu-west-1-a, will give shortburn 5m. Patch command: `releasectl traffic-split --shard eu-west-1-a --from v2.13.0 --to v2.12.8 --pct 10`

olivia: also spinning repro load locally with PROD-like tokens + hot-cache and cold-cache. Sharing repro script: ```bash
# repro load
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -sS -X POST 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROD_TEST_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"hello world","max_tokens":64}' 
    https://api.redwood/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.015
done
wait
```

samir: after routing 10% back to v2.12.8 p99 dropped to ~260ms on that cohort — suggests runtime change is causal. Nice catch.

kerry: temporary mitigation options: 1) rollback v2.13.0 on eu-west-1-a fully, 2) flip batching window back to 12ms (hotfix flag), or 3) disable kernel-selector experimental heuristic. Which is fastest?

ravi: flipping batching window is a config flip -> single-flag toggle, can push now as safe hotfix. Rolling back entire runtime will take longer (pods replace, cold starts).

olivia: agree — config flip first. Pushing hotfix: `runtimectl set-config --shard eu-west-1-a --key batching_window_ms --value 12`

ops-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: batching_window_ms set to 12ms on eu-west-1-a by ravi at 10:32 UTC.

samir: monitoring... p95 down to ~210ms, p99 down to ~300ms after flag flip. Customer confirmations coming in. Looks like aggressive batching reduction in v2.13 increased context-switches on certain kernels for sequences ~512.

kerry: follow-ups: - create a regression test in canary that simulates seq lengths 400-800 with mix of short tokens - add a guard in kernel selector to detect pathological seq distribution and fallback - release a patched v2.13.1 with config default safe value

olivia: opening a ticket with triage notes + repro artifacts and assigning to eng-runtime. Ticket: https://tickets.redwood/RT-4219

support-bot: NOTE: notified affected customers and offered temporary routing to older runtime.

samir: summary of immediate action items: 1) keep batching_window_ms at 12ms on eu-west-1-a until v2.13.1 releases (ravi) 2) create canary regression (olivia) 3) patch kernel selector heuristic (eng-runtime) 4) customers informed (support)

kerry: thanks team. If p99 re-spikes after hotfix we fallback to full rollback. Keeping this thread as the single source of truth for the triage.

samir: adding logs snippet that showed the pathological delays (stacked generators waiting on kernel selection): ```
2026-03-17T10:12:45Z runtime[pid=2231] WARN kernel_selector: selected kernel=matmul_v2 heur=aggressive latency_est=4.5ms
2026-03-17T10:12:45Z runtime[pid=2231] INFO serve: queuing request id=abc123 seq_len=520 batch_size=1
2026-03-17T10:12:46Z runtime[pid=2231] DEBUG perf: context_switch_wait=18ms kernel_prep=120ms exec=560ms
```

olivia: saved logs and repro traces in the ticket. Good job.

ravi: keeping watchers updated, will schedule full rollback playbook if needed.

kerry: closing loop — mark as resolved when v2.13.1 deployed canary and p95/p99 are back to baseline on cohort checks. :white_check_mark:
